title: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.22248v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to reason over behavioral evidence, but existing LLM-based approaches to passive sensing have largely continued to rely on task-specific fine-tuning or sensor-specific pretraining. In this paper, we introduce \textbf{OAK-Mind}, a zer\textbf{O}-training, multi-\textbf{A}gent, \textbf{K}nowledge-grounded LLM pipeline for inferring mental health changes from passive sensing data. The pipeline organizes sensing data into behavioral dimensions including sleep, physical activity, location mobility, and smartphone use, and orchestrates specialized agents grounded in mental health literature to interpret longitudinal behavioral

translated_title: OAK-Mind：基于知识驱动的多智能体大语言模型实现零训练的被动感知心理健康变化推断
translated_abstract: 可穿戴设备和智能手机传感器能够捕捉与心理健康相关的行为信号，然而从这些信号推断心理健康结果传统上依赖于需要标注数据的监督式模型，且这些模型对其预测所提供的洞察十分有限。大语言模型（LLM）为基于行为证据进行推理提供了新的机会，但现有的基于LLM的被动感知方法在很大程度上仍依赖于任务特定的微调或传感器特定的预训练。在本文中，我们提出了OAK-Mind，这是一个零训练、多智能体、知识驱动的LLM流水线，用于从被动感知数据中推断心理健康变化。该流水线将感知数据组织成多个行为维度，包括睡眠、身体活动、位置移动和智能手机使用，并协调多个以心理健康文献为知识基础的专业智能体来解读纵向行为数据。
tldr: OAK-Mind提出了一种零训练、多智能体、知识驱动的LLM流水线，无需标注数据或任务特定微调，通过基于心理健康文献解读睡眠、活动、移动等多维被动感知数据来推断心理健康变化。
en_tdlr: OAK-Mind is a zero-training, multi-agent, knowledge-grounded LLM pipeline that infers mental health changes from passive sensing data without labeled data or task-specific fine-tuning, by orchestrating literature-grounded agents to interpret behavioral dimensions such as sleep, physical activity, mobility, and smartphone use.
